content:
fitzgen opened PR #15317 from fitzgen:main-backport-a81c82ebe3 to bytecodealliance:main:

AsyncWriteStream::write queued every buffer it was handed, including empty ones. A zero-length write consumes no check_write budget, so the budget did not bound how many of them could be queued: each call pushed one Bytes slot onto the worker's VecDeque (and that deque never shrinks). A guest issuing output-stream.write with an empty list in a loop could therefore grow host memory without bound, especially while the background writer was parked on a backpressured destination.

Treat an empty write as a no-op. The background worker already did nothing with an empty buffer, so this is not observable to the guest. With empty writes dropped, every queued entry holds at least one byte of budget, so the queue length is bounded by the write budget.

GHSA-5m8g-xhq4-4h93
